columns.headline: Chad Hangs the Week's High on Joe G and Walks Away Whistling
columns.dek: Chad scored the week's best and Joe G the worst, in the same matchup. Elsewhere, Collin proved a winning lineup can exist on the bench of a losing team.
body: Chad scored 155.24 and Joe G scored 68.26, which is the kind of gap that usually requires one team to forget about the game entirely. The margin was 86.98, the biggest of the week by a wide stretch, and the series between them now sits tied 11-11. Chad's best possible lineup was 156.64, so he left almost nothing on the table. Joe G's best lineup was 81.36, so even perfection would have lost by a lot. CeeDee Lamb contributed 1.90 against a projection of 15.46, and RJ Harvey added 0.70 against 9.24. Joe G still sits fifth at 6-4, which says something about the rest of the league.

The closest game belongs to Collin and Jon, and it was ugly for both. Jon won 81.54 to 74.42, a 7.12 margin, and he did it without a single point sitting on his bench. Collin has no such defense. Jordan Love scored 25.28 on the bench while Tyler Shough, starting at quarterback, scored -0.16. Collin's best lineup came to 107.46, which would have beaten Jon outright. He is now last at 2-8, so at least the self-inflicted wound was consistent.

Jeff climbed from ninth to sixth by beating Brad 108.36 to 100.70, and he did it with Matthew Stafford at quarterback delivering 0.00 against a projection of 18.17. Jayden Daniels covered for him with 32.26. Mike Evans put up 22.80 on Jeff's bench and C.J. Stroud added 20.94, so there is a better team in there somewhere, but a win is a win. Jeff now sits at 5-5, and Brad still leads the series 10-7, which is a nice thing to have when the current score says otherwise.

The best start against projection came from TJ, whose Drake Maye scored 39.46 against 18.47 projected. That carried TJ to 123.56, third best of the week, and a win over Ben that moved TJ up to fourth. Ben dropped from seventh to tenth at 3-7. David Montgomery gave Ben 1.10 at running back, which is not a typo. Brad had his own version of this with Carnell Tate at 1.10 against 11.10 projected and Isaiah Likely's 26.90 was the only thing on that roster working at full volume.

The middle of the standings did the most shuffling. Joe K beat Kris 124.88 to 105.50 behind Puka Nacua's 29.20, jumping from tenth to seventh. Jeremiyah Love chipped in 2.20, which Joe K can have back as a souvenir. Kris lost, but still rose to third at 7-3, and left MarShawn Lloyd's 16.20 on the bench to think about it. Jared fell from sixth to ninth against Flanders, who won 96.34 to 85.92 even though Kenyon Sadiq gave the tight end slot 0.00.

Against the median of 100.25, six managers cleared the bar: Chad, Joe K, TJ, Jeff, Kris and Brad, who cleared it by the slimmest of margins at 100.70. Everyone else, Jon included, missed. At the top, Chad took first at 8-2 with Jon right behind at the same record. At the bottom, Collin holds last with Flanders climbing a spot to eleventh. The league looks settled on paper and nowhere near it in practice.
